summary.text: A 42-year-old non-smoking, non-alcoholic woman with no prior medical history presented to an outpatient department with bilateral breast pain and milky discharge lasting 18 months. Additional symptoms were headache, diplopia, blurred vision, skin darkening for one month and mild lower abdominal pain with heaviness. There was no history of nausea, vomiting, trauma or neurological deficits, and examination found no breast masses or axillary lymphadenopathy.

Laboratory tests including LFT, RFT, CBC and a pregnancy test were normal, but serum prolactin was markedly elevated at 2928 uIU/ml (normal 66-500 uIU/ml). Breast and axillary ultrasound were normal, abdominal ultrasound showed a 3.5 x 3.4 cm left ovarian dermoid cyst, and brain MRI identified a 4 x 4 mm hypo-enhancing lesion on the posterior left pituitary gland consistent with a pituitary microadenoma.

Based on clinical, biochemical and imaging findings, a diagnosis of pituitary microadenoma with a left ovarian dermoid cyst was made. The patient was treated with cabergoline 0.5 mg twice weekly for one year, resulting in significant improvement of breast tenderness and galactorrhea, with ongoing follow-up advised. The abstract also states the patient has been getting symptomatic treatment.
